segments.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: חוֹזְרַנִי עַל כׇּל צִדְדֵי חֲכָמִים וְלֹא מָצָאתִי אָדָם שֶׁהִשְׁוָה מִדּוֹתָיו בִּקְטַנָּה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר. שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּמְטַיֶּילֶת עִמּוֹ בֶּחָצֵר, וְעוֹמֶדֶת מֵחֵיקוֹ וְטוֹבֶלֶת וְאוֹכֶלֶת בִּתְרוּמָה לָעֶרֶב.
segments.en: § It is taught in the mishna: «Rabbi Elazar says:» The act of a minor girl is nothing. Rather, her status is as though she were a seduced unmarried woman. «Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said: I reviewed all the opinions of the Sages» concerning these matters, «and I did not find any person who applied a consistent standard with regard to a minor like Rabbi Elazar» did. «For Rabbi Elazar portrayed her as a girl walking with» her husband «in a courtyard, who stands up from his bosom» after he engaged in intercourse with her, «and immerses» herself to become ritually pure, «and partakes of teruma by evening» as if there were no marital bond between them and as if she, as the daughter of a priest, could continue to partake of teruma. The daughter of a priest is prohibited from eating teruma once she is married to a non-priest.
